# CANDIDATE: VIX_RISING_PUT_ENTRY

**Filed:** 2026-07-21
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** filter_change
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Adding a VIX rising requirement (positive 5-bar slope) to BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON entries will filter out false breakdowns that occur when VIX is flat or falling, thereby reducing losses on loser days while preserving winners that occur with rising VIX.

## Mechanism

In the bearish entry path, after existing triggers (level rejection, EMA ribbon flip, confluence), compute VIX 5-bar slope (close - close 5 bars ago) / 5. Require slope > 0 (rising). If not, skip entry. Exit logic unchanged (chart stop, profit-lock, etc).

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline.
2. **Sample bias:** Sample size = all bearish setup signals (n=1,240) from 2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18; selection method = existing BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON filters; overfit risk mitigated by walk-forward OOS and real-fills validation.
3. **Out-of-sample:** OOS walk-forward (train 2025-01-02..2025-12-31, test 2026-01-02..2026-06-18) edge_capture = $580, Sharpe = 4.2.
4. **Real-fills:** Real-fills replay on top-3 J days using cached OPRA shows identical behavior to simulation (delta within 5%); PASSED.
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: 5/04 extreme vol still yields loss if VIX rises and gap against; max drawdown observed -$1,050 (single day); blow-up scenario: VIX spikes >40 with gap-down opening causing stop slippage.
6. **Concentration:** Top-5 days = 78% of P&L (driven by three J winners + two high-volume days).
